### Product BOM setup and guided catalog builder

FenceOS stores the BOM catalog and product links, but the primary setup flow now lives on the product catalog pages.

- Org Admins can open **Organization > Products**, then choose **BOM Setup** at the top of that page.
- Super Admins can open an organization's settings page and then use **Manage Products & BOM** for that specific organization.
- FenceOS stores the BOM catalog and product mappings in its own database, per organization.
- Operator is the place where teams now run **Generate BOM**, **Regenerate BOM**, review the BOM output tabs, and save manual supplement edits.
- FenceOS provides a **BOM Builder** for safely authoring and publishing the organization-level catalog used by quote generation. Super Admins always have access; an Org Admin can use it only after a Super Admin enables **Allow Org Admins to manage Advanced BOM Catalog** for that organization.

The products-and-BOM flow has two layers:

- **Products** is where Org Admins create, edit, duplicate, group, and price fence products and gates.
- If an organization has no gates explicitly enabled, **Products** still lists the inherited gate templates that Field Estimator can use as its safe fallback and labels that state. Edit or duplicate one of those gates to establish organization-specific settings; the platform template itself remains unchanged.
- **Bulk Upload** on an org product page creates or updates org-owned fence types from the CSV template; it does not mutate the platform template library.
- **BOM Setup** is the org-admin mapping view where each FenceOS fence product gets tied to the BOM system and BOM style that should drive takeoffs.
- **Guided Builder** is the default. Choose **Create a new recipe**, **Edit an existing recipe**, or **Repair incomplete setup**, then answer the fence type, system, style, height, variant, section, post, gate, mapping, and review questions in order. The builder never asks for internal IDs, JSON, formula trees, or count-variable names.
- Choose a fence type first. When it has a saved mapping, the builder fills in its system, style, optional setup height, and available default variant. Review those choices before continuing. This does not change the catalog or save a mapping. Changing the system or style clears the previous height and variant choices.
- Styles are filtered to the chosen system. An incompatible saved style stays visible with **review scope** so you can deliberately correct it. **No variant** means the assembly has no variant; it is a separate choice from a named variant such as **standard**.
- **Advanced Editor** remains available from the same page for unusual formulas, rules, imports, bulk repair, and entity-level work. Both views edit the same local catalog draft, so switching views does not publish or discard changes.
- In **Advanced Editor → Fence Systems**, open a system to manage its optional **Material Variants**. Add the names that are meaningful for that system—for example Cedar or Treated for wood; White, Tan, Adobe, Maple, Walnut, Green, or Teak for vinyl; Black, Bronze, or Almond for aluminum; and Black or Galvanized for chain-link. A new Fence System starts with no named variants until you add them.
- Existing Fence Systems that have not adopted a system-owned list continue to show the legacy inferred choices. Adding or removing a choice converts that system to an explicit list. Removing a choice never deletes or rewrites saved assembly recipes or fence-type mappings; an older saved value remains visible as needing review until an admin deliberately updates it. Choose **Use no named variants** only when the system truly should not vary.
- For a full advanced CSV catalog import, `systems.csv` may include a trailing `variants` column with pipe-separated names such as `White|Tan|Adobe`. Legacy three-column `systems.csv` packets remain accepted and leave those imported systems on legacy inferred choices.
- In **Organization Settings → Platform setup → Feature rollouts**, a Super Admin can use the **Allow Org Admins to manage Advanced BOM Catalog** checkbox. It is off by default. Org Admins cannot enable it themselves or use it to manage another organization.

#### Recipe quantities and review

- **How BOM setup works** can be opened at any time. It does not change the catalog or automatically open on first use.
- A post recipe always means materials for **one post**. The drawing already supplies the project counts for line, corner, end, and gate posts; FenceOS multiplies each matching one-post recipe by that count exactly once. Do not place the drawing post-count variable inside a post recipe. Guided Builder accepts only per-post quantities, and shared validation rejects a matching post-count formula from Advanced Editor.
- Gate-post materials belong in the **one gate post** recipe. Gate leaf, frame, and hardware belong in a separate gate recipe for each supported type, opening width, installed height, and variant. Guided Builder uses one wood gate family for the selected fence style because the saved fence-type mapping and live resolver carry one family; changing it updates every configured wood gate in that guided scope. A gate recipe cannot reference the same matching gate-count variable by which the engine multiplies that gate assembly.
- When an existing style has different recipes by height or variant, **Edit an existing recipe** shows **Editing materials for** with the active height and variant. Opening an existing recipe or repair step does not modify its catalog rows. A missing gate recipe stays empty instead of showing materials from another height. Changes apply only to that cell; the other combinations remain unchanged and must all be complete before review.
- **Round up to package** requires a positive package size. Productless placeholder rows stay provisional and do not create empty catalog assemblies.
- Product search in Guided Builder matches any part of the full product name or SKU. If more than 25 products match, it shows the match count and asks you to narrow the search. A new orderable product requires name, SKU, unit, and category. Duplicate SKUs remain possible only after explicit confirmation; FenceOS never substitutes a product based on name or SKU.
- The **Connect the fence type** step shows system and style names and lets you choose an available default variant without typing identifiers or labels. The default variant must be included in the recipes being reviewed. An older or different default stays visible until you deliberately choose a reviewed variant or go back and include that default in your recipe choices. If no matching recipe exists, the scope step keeps that current default available and explains that its recipe needs to be built. It preserves the organization's complete mapping set. **Setup height (optional)** is setup information; actual takeoff quantities always use the height saved on the drawing. If **Continue** is disabled, the builder explains what still needs to be completed. The height-and-variant selector marks incomplete combinations with **needs materials**, so you can find unfinished recipes directly.
- Review runs a labeled sample drawing through the shared resolver, takeoff engine, and rule evaluator. It shows per-instance recipe quantities, drawing counts, resulting quantities, blockers, and matching rule effects before persistence.
- Guided publish previews and stores the full catalog plus complete mapping set together under one combined revision and an exact-content preview receipt. If either stored input or the reviewed payload changes after preview, FenceOS stores neither half, keeps the local edits, and requires a fresh preview.
- The **Recipe Lines** tab presents the catalog's component records as a compact table in their saved assembly-and-recipe order. Search accepts any part of the product name, SKU, product ID, assembly title, component ID, or component role. The count reports all matches, while the table initially renders the first 50; choose **Show all** when the full matching list is needed. Choose **Edit recipe line** to open its focused editor. The active line stays visible even if an edit no longer matches the search, and newly added or duplicated lines open without clearing the search.
- Recipe-line status comes from the same catalog validation used by **Review & Publish**. Missing product or assembly references and duplicate component IDs are called out in the table. **View row** beside a recipe-line issue switches to and focuses that row, **View assembly** opens an overlapping or invalid assembly, and **View rule** opens the affected rule when a rule action points to a missing product. If Review & Publish reports only the known BidRight chain-link defects (a 6-foot section stored as 5 feet, or a duplicated 4-by-10 gate), **Repair known catalog defects** applies that correction to the draft so you can retry.
- Each BOM Product reports both recipe-line usage and rule-action references. Expand the usage disclosure to see assembly titles, rule names, and their reference counts; products with neither kind of dependency show **Not used by any recipe lines or rules**.
- A product that is still referenced by a recipe line or rule cannot be deleted. Replace or remove those dependencies first. Editing a valid Product ID preserves its existing recipe-line and rule references in the local draft, while blank or duplicate IDs stay uncommitted so they cannot break the catalog graph.
- If the stored template pack fails to load, BOM Builder blocks both views and shows **Retry** instead of presenting a blank catalog. Fence-type or mapping-data failures still allow recipe repair but block guided mapping and final review. The emergency **Raw JSON Fallback** is available only to Super Admins in Advanced Editor; enabled Org Admins stay in the structured tools.

#### Recipe heights, variants and post roles

- Variants and saved style heights are selected from the compatible catalog choices in assemblies and Fence Type Mappings. A Fence System's explicit Material Variants are the primary choices; systems that have not adopted a list retain the legacy material defaults. Existing out-of-list values stay visible for deliberate repair instead of being silently remapped.
- **Fence Styles → Heights (feet, comma separated)** accepts lists such as `4, 4.5, 5, 6`; commas and partial decimals stay in place while you type. Style summaries, assembly height choices, mapping choices, and Guided Builder height choices show feet, including **4.5 ft** for 54 inches and **6 ft** for 72 inches. Invalid entries must be corrected before publishing.
- Product heights are the choices offered to estimators. BOM style heights declare recipe coverage, and each assembly supplies materials for its exact height. To offer 54″, add **4.5** to the fence product and BOM style, then configure the matching section, post, and gate recipes. Adding a style height alone does not create those recipes. The height saved on the drawing selects the takeoff; a setup default does not override it. Existing storage, raw JSON, CSV, and formula heights remain in feet (`54″ = 4.5`, `72″ = 6`), and existing quotes are unchanged. Estimator and customer quote height labels retain their current feet presentation.
- In **Advanced Editor**, assemblies can be assigned to more than one style. Leave style scope blank only for shared post assemblies that should apply across the matching system. A matching style-specific post assembly replaces the shared assembly for that post role; FenceOS does not stack both recipes. Two equally specific matches block publishing or generation until the overlap is corrected. Component role is advanced metadata; normal takeoff accuracy comes from the assembly type, product, per-instance quantity formula, and rounding rule.
- Product categories continue to describe the physical item, such as post, rail, picket, fastener, concrete, or hardware. Line, corner, end, and gate-post behavior belongs to the assembly type; do not create separate physical product categories just to represent those post roles.

### How product BOM links work

FenceOS does not guess which BOM recipe to use from a display name alone. Each FenceOS fence type must be mapped explicitly.

- Open the relevant fence product and choose the matching **Fence System** and **BOM Style**.
- Optionally choose a default variant and one of the style's supported heights, then set the wood gate build system and notes when applicable.
- Quotes only generate a full BOM when the fence types used in the drawing have matching BOM template coverage.
- Gates require an explicit type and width from the drawing. Wood mappings that select **Insta Gate** or **Wood Frame** require an exact assembly for that family, style, installed height, width, and type; FenceOS does not silently substitute a 4-foot single gate or another family.
- If a quote has enough coverage for fence and post materials but has incomplete gate details or is missing an exact gate material assembly, Operator shows the BOM as **Mixed** and keeps the generated fence/post rows visible for review. **Mixed** and **Failed** BOMs are never order-ready. Correct the drawing or catalog, or add reviewed manual supplement items, before ordering.
- A straight, continuous junction between two drawn segments uses one line post. Corner posts are used where the fence turns, end posts where a run physically stops, and gate posts at gate openings.
- Guided **Review catalog and mappings** checks selected-scope readiness, global catalog validity, sample takeoff quantities, stored-versus-draft entity counts, and the exact server-authoritative mapping diff. **Confirm catalog and mappings publish** stores both datasets in one transaction. Advanced Editor keeps its catalog-focused **Review & Publish** action for expert repair.
- FenceOS publishes against the catalog revision captured by that preview. If another window changes the catalog first, FenceOS makes no replacement, keeps the local edits intact, and asks for **Re-run Preview**.
- Validation failures stay beside **Review & Publish** as an itemized list with the affected product, assembly, or other catalog row. Correct the named rows and choose **Retry**, or use **Repair known catalog defects** when FenceOS can apply the BidRight chain-link height and duplicate-gate correction; the draft is not cleared.
- After **Confirm Publish** completes, the structured catalog and its row counts remain visible; the confirmation reports how many mappings were preserved or dropped, and a browser refresh is not required.
- Publishing the advanced catalog preserves saved product BOM links when the referenced BOM system and style IDs still exist in the saved catalog. If a catalog edit removes or renames those IDs, remap the affected products against the current system and style rows.
